hardware: Apple M3; 10-core GPU, eight CPU cores, 16 GB RAM
changes: First-page contiguous histograms accumulate directly in their integer-cache destination. The existing integer-statistics kernel materializes the binary64 view. Discontiguous output and later-page accumulation retain the staging path. Arithmetic, tie rules, precision and command timing boundaries are unchanged.

A Page-owned column-major byte cache accelerates repeated partition gathers on large narrow compressed pages using the existing transpose and classifier kernels. Initialization/publication uses std::call_once. The canonical compressed page remains unchanged for histogram, prediction, restoration and export.

Column-cache eligibility: dense eight-bit compressed page with 256 symbols, stride equal to feature count, 4..64 features, at least 2^20 rows, and a contiguous full head or tail buffer. Each cache is bounded by min(512 MiB, recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize/32). Other pages use the existing compressed classifier.

final_candidate.command: bash scripts/test.sh --native metal_integer_cache_api metal_compressed_consumers_api metal_inmemory_ellpack_api metal_ordinary_ellpack_api metal_partition --python tests/test_metal_training.py tests/test_metal_workflows.py tests/test_metal_prediction.py tests/test_metal_direct_ellpack.py tests/test_metal_inmemory_ellpack.py tests/test_metal_external_host.py tests/test_metal_distributed_training.py --log-dir results/memory-partition-20261107T012759Z/column-check

new_checks: 108 histogram output-layout/page cases, plus existing 48 integer-cache cases: nonzero offsets, contiguous/gapped/reversed outputs, empty nodes, replacement/accumulation, exact integer sums and untouched guards. The new layout oracle also passed against the original baseline library.

Large compressed page cases cover full-head/full-tail ownership after the source cache is destroyed, split-buffer and row-count boundary fallbacks, concurrent first use, cache reuse, numeric/category splits, complete/partial/unordered row ranges, and poisoned/absent host mirrors.

limits: Three CPU/baseline-MPS/candidate-MPS repeats for each 100-round workload; rotated order, fresh processes, warmed runtime, eight CPU threads, depth 6 and 256 bins. Training includes quantization, optional column-cache construction and held-out evaluation each round. Loading, DMatrix creation and final prediction are separate.
The 1000-round HIGGS confirmation has only one run per variant. It is a long correctness/performance check, not a three-repeat median.

No builds, tests or other benchmarks from this task overlapped training timings. Other applications and system-wide paging were not controlled. All repeats and regressions are retained; do not mix ratios across sessions.
The column cache adds memory on eligible narrow pages; it is excluded on the wide workload. Resource allocation savings do not establish lower peak physical footprint.

Memory diagnostics separately sample Metal currentAllocatedSize and task_vm_info after each iteration, plus process lifetime physical-footprint peak. Their timings are instrumented single runs and are not the training acceptance medians. They do not measure total system GPU memory.

Counter families may overlap. Partition command boundaries are unchanged; initial column transposition is counted separately by index_gpu_time_ns and included in whole training time. Do not sum family durations or infer CPU time by subtraction.

Before/after MPS equality and same-model CPU prediction checks do not establish independently trained CPU/MPS equivalence. Quality differences are recorded. Zero-valued counters are omitted from compact worker records.
